sentences.text: Petitioner is the 1st accused in Crime No.107 of 2022 of Kaipamangalam Police Station, Thrissur District, alleging commission of offences under Sections 341, 323, 324, 506(1), 498A, 420 and 308 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

The allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner, after his marriage with the defacto complainant, had subjected the defacto complainant to mental and physical cruelty with a demand for dowry.
It is also alleged that on one particular day, the petitioner attempted to commit the offence under Section 308 of the IPC by tying a shawl around the neck of the defacto complainant.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the allegations against the petitioner are totally baseless.

It is submitted that while there are other matrimonial disputes between the petitioner and the defacto complainant, the petitioner did not have any occasion to commit the offence under Section 498A of the IPC.

It is submitted that the allegation in respect of the offence under Section 308 IPC is that on 28.01.2022, the petition had attempted to tie a shawl around the neck of the defacto complainant and attempted to strangulate her.
It is submitted that the allegation is absolutely false.
It is submitted that the defacto complainant/victim was using a cervical collar which is evident from Annexure A1 photograph taken in the month of December 2021.

It is submitted that by mis-using the fact that certain marks were there on the neck of the defacto complainant owing to use of the cervical collar, she had cooked up a story that the petitioner had attempted to strangulate her.

It is submitted that investigation has been completed and a final report has already been filed and the matter is now pending as S.C.No.985 of 2022 on the file of Assistant Sessions Court, Irinjalakuda.
It is submitted that the petitioner has been in custody from 05.10.2023 and that the continued detention of the petitioner is, therefore, not necessary in the facts and circumstances of the case.
3. The learned Public Prosecutor opposes the grant of bail.
Circumstances of the case appearing against the petitioner are pointed out to show that the petitioner is not entitled to bail.
It is confirmed that a final report has already been filed.

It is submitted that the Investigating Officer had already conducted further investigation after the filing of the initial final report and following the said investigation a further report has also been filed before the court.
Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, I am of the view that the petitioner can be granted bail subject to conditions.
No criminal antecedents are reported against the petitioner.
The allegations against the petitioner are as noticed above.
The investigation has been completed and final report has already been filed.
Further detention of the petition does not appear to be necessary in such circumstances.

Therefore, the petitioner shall be released on bail subject to the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall execute a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court;
